extracted.intended_audience: companies, small businesses, and PR professionals seeking to distribute press releases via Cision PR Newswire (or similar newswire services)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for preparing and submitting a press release to Cision PR Newswire, covering content, formatting, account/submission requirements, and stylistic conventions to maximize acceptance and reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abide by distributor content guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Your newswire submission will need to meet the company’s content guidelines before they will publish it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributor must know the content does not subvert their company values. Read the distributor's terms of use and content policies to avoid creating unusable content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear language
rubrics_metrics.description: Be transparent in what you are trying to promote and provide reliable sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clear, transparent language makes you appear more trustworthy and provides a better platform for explaining your message to the target audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid sensationalism
rubrics_metrics.description: Content should be truthful and verifiable without making assumptions that could cause PR Newswire to fall into disrepute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use exaggerated, unsubstantiated claims or clickbait phrasing that misleads readers or the distributor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uphold ethical standards / do not mislead
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not attempt to mislead the reader, and ensure you are not aiming to cause harm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ethical norms and the distributor's terms of use; misleading or harmful content may be rejected or cause reputational issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match the distributor’s format and tone
rubrics_metrics.description: Format and tone should align with the distributor's expectations to speed processing and improve visibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhering to the expected style makes the release easier to read and more likely to be accepted and distributed widely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline: follow SEO and length guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Headline should match most SEO guidelines: draw clicks, use action verbs, and inform users why they should pay attention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep headlines no more than 100 characters; use verbs that suggest action and make value/interest clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the city from which the release is officially originating and the date you are releasing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dateline signals origin and timing; format per distributor/journalist expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph: answer the five whys
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead paragraph should answer Who, What, When, Where, Why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the AIDA method (Attention, Interest, Desire, Action) to organize the lead can draw more interest and start telling a story that drives engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Press release body: structure and content
rubrics_metrics.description: The body contains all supporting details, including quotes, context, short paragraphs that each communicate one idea, and calls-to-action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize information logically; each short paragraph should convey a single idea. Include contextual details and clear CTAs where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep body concise (~500 words)
rubrics_metrics.description: The body should top out at around 500 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer releases become less concise and clear; staying near 500 words helps clarity and engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include quotes and verifiable data
rubrics_metrics.description: Information such as quotes and verifiable data can help back up anything you say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authoritative, attributable quotes and include verifiable facts or data to support claims; avoid unsubstantiated assertions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Boilerplate at end of release
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefly describe the company sending the release at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include organization values or ambitions to help readers understand focus; keep it short and informative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: Include contact details enabling people to contact the business sending the release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact info may be part of CTAs; ensure media and others can reach a representative for follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comply with AP style conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Adhere to AP Style to match professional journalistic writing standards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key AP style points called out: avoid the Oxford comma in lists unless necessary; spell out numbers from one to nine; capitalize formal titles when used alongside names (e.g., Vice President Harris); use a specific format for dates and times; spell out the first reference of most abbreviations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include required submission fields in UI
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting via the PR Newswire dashboard, include recipients/distribution channels, press release headline, dateline and boilerplate, and press release body text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also format the message, add URLs and boilerplate information as necessary before sending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upload multimedia to increase engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: PR Newswire UI allows uploading images, videos, and other media with the press release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multimedia can increase engagement and visibility further; include relevant images, videos, and URLs when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use targeting options to reach the right audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Take advantage of targeting to reach specific industries, geographic regions, or audience demographics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targeting helps ensure your message reaches the most relevant journalists and media outlets rather than a generic blast.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an account and authenticate submitters
rubrics_metrics.description: You must create an account and confirm who in your company can submit releases so the business can be contacted and submissions authenticated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PR Newswire requires membership before sending messages; membership costs noted on the page (e.g., $195/year, $50 more if paid by invoice). Authentication prevents unauthorized submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track performance with analytics and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: PR Newswire offers analytics and reporting on the performance of distributed press releases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use reporting to monitor views, engagement, and pick-up rates, and to refine targeting and messaging for future releases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format for discoverability and pick-up (SEO/backlinks)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distribution through PR Newswire can improve search engine visibility through quality backlinks from reputable sites that may pick up your release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write headline and body with SEO in mind (concise headline, relevant keywords, proper URLs) to maximize pick-up and backlinks.
